claims.text: A DFT+CPA model with temperature-dependent dynamical defect-scattering corrections will predict electronic conductivity of bulk HfNbTaTiZr containing 1 wt.% oxygen with less than 5% error across 0–200 K and 300–1200 K.
The improved model will predict thermal conductivity of bulk HfNbTaTiZr containing 1 wt.% oxygen with less than 5% error across the specified temperature regimes.
A distinctive conductivity deviation near 700 K results from oxygen-induced defect scattering and activated defect motion.
Oxygen impurities in HfNbTaTiZr can be represented as point defects in a disordered alloy framework.
DFT combined with CPA and temperature-dependent dynamical corrections can capture both static chemical disorder and thermally activated defect motion.
The 0–200 K regime involves cryogenic electronic scattering, including quantum-interference effects.
The 300–1200 K regime involves thermally activated defect motion and phonon scattering.
Oxygen impurities induce local lattice distortions in HfNbTaTiZr.
Oxygen-induced local distortions influence the electronic structure through band broadening and localized states.
Including oxygen-defect scattering and dynamical corrections modifies the local electronic structure and phonon spectra.
Changes in local electronic structure and phonon spectra alter percolative pathways for charge and heat transport.
Accounting for oxygen defects and temperature-dependent dynamics remedies deficiencies associated with defect-free transport models.
The model will predict conductivity with less than 5% error for both a defect-free sample and a sample containing 1 wt.% oxygen.
Traditional defect-free predictions will have more than 15% conductivity error near 700 K.
Existing perfect-crystal analytical predictions with simplified scattering mechanisms typically exceed 15% conductivity error, particularly for oxygen-doped specimens.
The proposed approach is applicable to bulk HfNbTaTiZr from 0–200 K and 300–1200 K at oxygen concentrations up to 1 wt.%.
The model's reliability may diminish outside the specified temperature ranges or above 1 wt.% oxygen.
Rare-event dynamical correlations, many-body effects, additional scattering processes, or nonlinear defect interactions may require treatment beyond the proposed corrections.
Failure to reproduce the conductivity behavior near 700 K within the stated tolerance would indicate that the proposed scattering treatment is insufficient.

contradictions.description: The target is less than 5% error, but the falsification rule parenthetically equates failure of a ±5% match with error exceeding 15%. Errors between 5% and 15% therefore have no consistent classification.
The predicted 700 K feature is described only as a drop or shift, whereas the falsification rule requires anticipated non-monotonic behavior. A drop or shift need not be non-monotonic.
